title: Keyfactor Surpasses $200 Million ARR Amid Enterprise Post-Quantum Migration Surge - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Keyfactor's ARR crossed $200 million (doubling in under two years, +35% YoY) on the back of a $1 billion-plus Summit Partners investment and a planned Cofide acquisition for AI-agent identity, as U.S. federal post-quantum-cryptography migration mandates ahead of the 2030 deadline drive triple-digit growth in certificate volumes across top banks, retailers and Fortune 100 firms.

insights.claim: Keyfactor's annual recurring revenue surpassed $200 million at the beginning of Q3 2026, doubling its revenue scale in under two years after crossing $100 million ARR, sustaining 35% year-over-year growth.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A concrete, fast-growing revenue base shows post-quantum-migration compliance spend is already a real, monetizable enterprise budget line today, not just a future TAM story.
insights.quote: Doubling its revenue scale in under two years after crossing $100 million ARR
insights.locator: Machine identity security and cryptography management platform Keyfactor

insights.claim: In July 2026, Keyfactor secured a strategic growth investment exceeding $1 billion led by Summit Partners to expand its global footprint and accelerate acquisitions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A $1B+ check size signals large-scale institutional conviction in machine-identity and PQC infrastructure as a durable category, comparable to late-stage cybersecurity infrastructure rounds.
insights.quote: Keyfactor secured a $1 billion-plus strategic growth investment led by Summit Partners
insights.locator: The company's sustained 35% year-over-year revenue expansion

insights.claim: Keyfactor announced its intent to acquire UK-based Cofide to integrate SPIFFE/SPIRE-based workload identity verification for cloud-native environments and AI agents directly into its Trust Control Plane.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PQC and machine-identity vendors are bolting on AI-agent identity verification as an adjacent growth vector; watch for further consolidation in machine-identity-for-AI-agents.
insights.locator: the firm announced its intent to acquire UK-based Cofide

insights.claim: Demand is reinforced by the White House's June 2026 executive orders requiring federal agencies to expedite post-quantum cryptography migration ahead of a 2030 deadline; Keyfactor holds FedRAMP certification and serves defense units across NATO member states.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A hard regulatory deadline (2030) backed by a named federal executive order is a durable, policy-driven demand catalyst for the whole PQC-migration vendor cohort, not just Keyfactor.
insights.locator: Demand for Keyfactor's platform is driven by tightening regulatory mandates

insights.claim: Keyfactor reports serving 50% of top U.S. and European banks, 80% of top U.S. retailers, and over 40% of Fortune 100 enterprises, with active PKI certificates up over 200% versus 2025, EJBCA SaaS certificates up 168% versus 2025, and automated certificates up 207% versus 2024.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Triple-digit certificate-volume growth across the highest-value enterprise verticals is a leading indicator of how fast PQC migration is actually being executed, useful for benchmarking peers and TAM timing.
